text_blocks.snippet: While Lyme disease doesn't directly cause cancer, there's a complex relationship involving inflammation and potential links to certain types of cancer, particularly lymphoma and breast cancer. Chronic Lyme disease, characterized by persistent inflammation, can potentially create an environment where cancer development is more likely. Some studies have found evidence of the Lyme disease bacteria, Borrelia burgdorferi, in breast cancer tissue, suggesting a possible role in cancer progression.
